title: Transverse variables in completed monoid-ideal quotients
statement:
Let $Q$ be a fine saturated monoid, written additively [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], which is sharp: $0$ is its only invertible element; and let $H\subset Q$ be an ideal ($H+Q\subset H$), including $H=\varnothing$ and $H=Q$. Let $n\geq0$. Let $L$ be either a field $k$ or a Cohen ring $C$ with residue characteristic $p$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring]. Write $L[Q][t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ for the ring with basis monomials $z^qt^a$ and product $z^qz^{q'}=z^{q+q'}$. Let $B$ be its completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] at $(\mathfrak m_L,z^q\ (q\ne0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)$, where $\mathfrak m_k=0$ and $\mathfrak m_C=pC$, and put $K=(z^h:h\in H)B$.

Every class in $B/K$ has a unique expansion $\sum_{q\in Q\setminus H}a_q(t)z^q$ with $a_q(t)\in L[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]; the displayed power series are formal sums with the usual coefficientwise addition and convolution multiplication. Equivalently, a formal monoid series belongs to $K$ exactly when all its coefficients indexed by $Q\setminus H$ vanish. If $f\in B$ has nonzero coefficient at $z^0$ as an element of the domain $L[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$, multiplication by $f$ on $B/K$ is injective.

If $n\geq1$, multiplication by $t_1$ on $B/K$ is injective. In the Cohen-ring case, for every $\theta\in B$ satisfying $\theta-p\in(z^q\ (q\ne0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)B$, multiplication by $t_1$ on $B/(K+\theta B)$ is also injective.

proof.text: Sharpness makes $F=\{0\}$ a face of $Q$. Apply the face-sharpening theorem with this face: its sharpened monoid is $Q$ itself, so $Q^{\rm gp}$ is free abelian of finite rank. Integrality embeds $Q$ in it, and $Q\cap(-Q)=\{0\}$. The positive-grading lemma therefore gives a homomorphism $w:Q^{\rm gp}\to\mathbf Z$ with $w(q)>0$ for $q\ne0$. Give $P=Q\oplus\mathbf N^n$ the grading $W(q,e)=w(q)+\sum_i e_i$; it is strictly positive off $(0,0)$. The coefficient ring $L$ is a complete Noetherian local domain: this is immediate for a field, and for a Cohen ring it follows from its definition and the PID-Noetherian lemma. Applying the completion-coefficient theorem to $P$ and $L$ identifies the displayed completion $B$ with coefficient families $(c_{q,e})_{(q,e)\in P}$, with finite convolution product.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p.70, with the coefficient-family completion calculation; the positive grading is the explicit sharp-monoid separation used in that calculation.

proof.text: Regroup the coefficients as $a_q(t)=\sum_{e\in\mathbf N^n}c_{q,e}t^e\in L[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$. The power-series definition makes this regrouping bijective, and its convolution is exactly the product in the statement. Since $H+Q\subseteq H$, multiplication by every monomial in $H$ has support in $H$. Conversely, the finite-generation theorem for sharp monoid ideals gives generators $s_1,\ldots,s_r$ with $H=\bigcup_i(s_i+Q)$; assign each coefficient indexed by $q\in H$ to one such $s_i$ and divide the exponent by $s_i$. The resulting finite tuple of coefficient families shows that every family supported on $H$ lies in $(z^h:h\in H)B$. Hence the quotient has, uniquely, precisely the coefficients indexed by $Q\setminus H$, proving the expansion and the equivalent membership criterion (including $H=\varnothing$ and $H=Q$).

In the coefficient of $z^q$ in $fx$, a term with a positive $Q$-exponent from $f$ would require an $x$-coefficient of strictly smaller degree. It is either zero because its exponent lies in $H$, or zero by minimality. Thus that coefficient is $g(t)a_q(t)$. It must vanish because $q

In a product of two nonzero series, the coefficient at the sum of their least exponents is the product of their two least nonzero coefficients: every other candidate pair has larger sum. That coefficient is nonzero because $L$ is a domain. Therefore $g(t)a_q(t)

proof.text: If $n\ge1$, take $f=t_1$. Its $z^0$ coefficient is the nonzero power series $t_1$, so Step 3 gives injectivity of multiplication by $t_1$ on $B/K$. This also covers the trivial monoid $Q=\{0\}$, where the same least-degree argument is just the usual power-series argument.

source.place: Expose VIII, proof of Lemma 3.4.13(i), printed p.113.

proof.text: Assume now that $L=C$ and $\theta-p\in J=(z^q\ (q\ne0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)B$, and write $N=B/K$. The coefficient description gives an evaluation map $N\to N_0$ at $t_1=0$, whose kernel is $t_1N$; $N_0$ is the same coefficient quotient with variables $t_2,\ldots,t_n$. The $z^0$ coefficient of the image $\bar\theta$ is $p+h(t_2,\ldots,t_n)$ with $h$ in the ideal generated by those variables, so it is nonzero in the domain $C[[t_2,\ldots,t_n]]$. The argument of Step 3, with $n-1$ variables, shows that multiplication by $\bar\theta$ on $N_0$ is injective. If $t_1x=\theta y$ in $N$, reduction gives $\bar\theta\bar y=0$, hence $y=t_1y_1$. Then $t_1(x-\theta y_1)=0$; Step 4 gives $x=\theta y_1$. Thus $t_1$ is injective on $N/\theta N$. For $n=0$ the assertion is vacuous, and the cases $H=Q$ and $H=\varnothing$ are already covered by the same coefficient argument.

split_report.summary: No new nodes. Read ILO VI 1.6 and VIII 3.4.13, checked the exact hypotheses, and expanded the coefficient-family completion model into a five-step proof. The first three steps establish the quotient expansion and regularity by a positive monoid grading; the fourth specializes to t_1; the fifth proves the Cohen equation quotient by reducing modulo t_1 and applying the same regularity argument to the reduced equation. Edge cases n=0, H=empty, H=Q, and Q={0} were checked.
